source: ICAI CA Foundation Paper 4 MCQ booklets with answer keys (icai.org, 'MCQ Questions and Keys')
note: Only for the trap reel. Answers are ICAI's official keys; 'trap' is our reading of the tempting wrong option.

questions.text: Due to an increase in price of product X from ₹100 to ₹110, quantity supplied increases from 150 units to 200 units. Calculate elasticity of supply using the arc-elasticity method. (a) 2.3 (b) 3 (c) 3.33 (d) 3.5
questions.trap_why: they use the point method, (50/150) ÷ (10/100) = 3.33, but the arc method divides by the averages: (50/175) ÷ (10/105) = 3

questions.text: When price is ₹20 the quantity demanded is 9 units, and when price is ₹19 the quantity demanded is 10 units. What is the marginal revenue from increasing output from 9 units to 10 units? (a) ₹20 (b) ₹19 (c) ₹10 (d) ₹1
questions.trap_why: they take the new price ₹19 as MR, but MR is the change in total revenue: 10 × 19 − 9 × 20 = 190 − 180 = ₹10

questions.text: From: operating surplus ₹2,500 cr, mixed income of self-employed ₹1,500 cr, rent ₹680 cr, profit ₹720 cr, interest ₹1,100 cr, net indirect tax ₹400 cr, consumption of fixed capital ₹300 cr, compensation of employees ₹1,000 cr — calculate GDP at market price. (a) ₹5,700 crores (b) ₹8,200 crores (c) ₹5,000 crores (d) ₹7,500 crores
questions.trap_why: they add rent, profit and interest again, but these are already inside operating surplus: 2,500 + 1,500 + 1,000 + 400 + 300 = 5,700

questions.text: The cost of producing 500 units is ₹25,000. The entrepreneur has invested ₹1,50,000 in the business and the normal market return is 10%. The selling price at which the firm will earn supernormal profit is: (a) ₹78 (b) ₹80 (c) ₹82 (d) ₹76
questions.trap_why: ₹80 only covers all costs including the ₹15,000 normal return, which is just normal profit; supernormal profit needs a price above ₹80, so ₹82

questions.text: The price of 1 kg of tea is ₹50 and 10 kg of tea is demanded. If the price of coffee rises from ₹30 to ₹40 per kg, the quantity demanded of tea rises from 10 kg to 15 kg. What is the cross price elasticity of tea? (a) +1 (b) −1.5 (c) +1.5 (d) −1
questions.trap_why: they put a minus sign out of habit, but tea and coffee are substitutes, so the cross elasticity is positive: 50% ÷ 33.3% = +1.5

questions.text: Calculate currency with the public: notes in circulation ₹45,000 cr, circulation of rupee coins ₹1,500 cr, circulation of small coins ₹750 cr, cash on hand with banks ₹27,500 cr. (a) ₹74,750 cr (b) ₹19,750 cr (c) ₹73,250 cr (d) ₹29,750 cr
questions.trap_why: they add the banks' cash, but cash held by banks is not with the public, so it is subtracted: 45,000 + 1,500 + 750 − 27,500 = 19,750

questions.text: Calculate the equilibrium level of income if the saving function is S = −20 + 0.25Y and autonomous investment (I) = ₹100 crores. (a) 320 crores (b) 160 crores (c) 480 crores (d) 240 crores
questions.trap_why: they drop the minus sign and solve 0.25Y = 100 − 20, but S = I gives −20 + 0.25Y = 100, so 0.25Y = 120 and Y = 480

questions.text: Calculate the average propensity to save when C = 300 and Y = 1,200. (a) 0.25 (b) 0.50 (c) 0.75 (d) 0.80
Units 1–5 have total revenue ₹100, 180, 240, 300, 330 and average revenue ₹100, 90, 80, 75, 66. Calculate the marginal revenue of the 4th unit. (a) ₹75 (b) ₹80 (c) ₹66 (d) ₹60
questions.trap_why: they read ₹75 off the AR column, but MR of the 4th unit is the rise in TR: 300 − 240 = ₹60

questions.text: The price of a product is ₹100 per unit. If price falls by 20% the quantity increases by 120 units. The price elasticity of demand is −1. The new quantity demanded due to the fall in price is: (a) 480 units (b) 600 units (c) 680 units (d) 720 units
questions.trap_why: 600 is the old quantity (120 is 20% of 600); the question asks for the new quantity, 600 + 120 = 720

questions.text: Money supply (M) is ₹500 crores, velocity (V) is 5 and the number of transactions (T) is 10,000. Calculate the average price level (P). (a) ₹25 thousand (b) ₹25 lakhs (c) ₹50 lakhs (d) ₹50 thousand
questions.trap_why: the digits are right but the unit slips: P = MV ÷ T = ₹2,500 crore ÷ 10,000 = ₹0.25 crore = ₹25 lakhs

questions.text: Calculate the arc elasticity if P1 = ₹15, P2 = ₹20, Q1 = 50 units and Q2 = 75 units. (a) 1.4 (b) 1.2 (c) 2.1 (d) 1.5
questions.trap_why: the point method gives (25/50) ÷ (5/15) = 1.5, but arc elasticity uses the averages: (25/62.5) ÷ (5/17.5) = 1.4

questions.text: Calculate gross value added at market price if sales = 750, opening stock = 300, closing stock = 200 and intermediate consumption = 250. (a) 400 (b) 450 (c) 600 (d) 650
questions.trap_why: stock fell by 100, so the change in stock is −100, not +100: 750 − 100 − 250 = 400

questions.text: Given the saving function S = −20 + 0.5Y and autonomous investment I = ₹100 crores, what is the consumption? (a) ₹240 crores (b) ₹140 crores (c) ₹340 crores (d) ₹440 crores
questions.trap_why: ₹240 crores is the equilibrium income; consumption is income minus saving: 240 − 100 = 140

questions.text: If the change in quantity demanded is 60% and the change in advertisement expenditure is 20%, what is the advertisement elasticity? (a) 3 (b) 0.33 (c) 6 (d) 20
questions.trap_why: they divide the wrong way round; elasticity is the response over the cause: 60% ÷ 20% = 3

questions.text: Calculate the subsidies when national income is ₹4,500 crore, NNP at market price is ₹4,800 crore and indirect taxes are ₹350 crore. (a) ₹400 crore (b) ₹650 crore (c) ₹50 crore (d) ₹100 crore
questions.trap_why: NI = NNP at MP − indirect taxes + subsidies, so 4,500 = 4,800 − 350 + S and S = 50, not 4,800 + 350 − 4,500

questions.text: With a money multiplier of 1.5 there has been an increase of ₹600 crore in money supply. Find the monetary base. (a) ₹800 cr (b) ₹200 cr (c) ₹400 cr (d) ₹900 cr
questions.trap_why: they multiply 600 × 1.5, but money supply = multiplier × base, so base = 600 ÷ 1.5 = 400

questions.text: When price is ₹30 the quantity demanded is 19 units and when price is ₹28 the quantity demanded is 20 units. What is the marginal revenue from increasing output from 19 to 20 units? (a) ₹10 (b) −₹10 (c) ₹20 (d) −₹20
questions.trap_why: total revenue falls from 570 to 560, so MR is −₹10; dropping the minus gives the trap

questions.text: Real GDP is ₹4,500 crore and nominal GDP is ₹6,750 crore. Calculate the GDP deflator. (a) 150 (b) 66.67 (c) 120 (d) 80.33
questions.trap_why: they divide real by nominal; the deflator is nominal ÷ real × 100 = 6,750 ÷ 4,500 × 100 = 150

questions.text: Investment expenditure increases by ₹300 crores and the marginal propensity to consume is 0.6. Calculate the total increase in income. (a) ₹300 crores (b) ₹100 crores (c) ₹650 crores (d) ₹750 crores
questions.trap_why: income rises by more than the investment; multiplier = 1 ÷ (1 − 0.6) = 2.5, so 300 × 2.5 = 750

questions.text: The monetary base is ₹250 crores and the money supply is ₹1,000 crores. Calculate the money multiplier. (a) 0.25 (b) 1 (c) 4 (d) 0.40
questions.trap_why: they divide base by supply; the multiplier is money supply ÷ base = 1,000 ÷ 250 = 4

questions.text: Output increases from 60 units to 70 units, and total revenue increases from ₹100 to ₹120. What is the marginal revenue? (a) ₹10 (b) ₹20 (c) ₹100 (d) ₹2
questions.trap_why: ₹20 is the change in total revenue for 10 extra units; per unit MR = 20 ÷ 10 = ₹2

questions.text: Calculate narrow money M1: currency with public ₹88,000 cr, demand deposits with banks ₹2,20,000 cr, time deposits with banks ₹2,40,000 cr, other deposits with RBI ₹2,60,000 cr, savings deposits with post office savings bank ₹50,000 cr. (a) ₹5,68,000 cr (b) ₹6,18,000 cr (c) ₹5,98,000 cr (d) ₹6,38,000 cr
questions.trap_why: post office savings deposits belong to M2, not M1: M1 = 88,000 + 2,20,000 + 2,60,000 = 5,68,000

questions.text: Calculate AR when MR = 15 and price elasticity of demand = 1.5. (a) 30 (b) 60 (c) 45 (d) 22.5
questions.trap_why: they multiply MR × e, but AR = MR × e ÷ (e − 1) = 15 × 1.5 ÷ 0.5 = 45

questions.text: If the reserve ratio is 0.10 and reserves increase by ₹1,000, what will be the change in the money supply? (a) ₹10,000 (b) ₹1,000 (c) ₹100 (d) ₹10
questions.trap_why: they multiply by the reserve ratio, but the multiplier is 1 ÷ 0.10 = 10, so 1,000 × 10 = ₹10,000

questions.text: Find the real GDP if nominal GDP = 720 and price index = 120. (a) 864 (b) 500 (c) 600 (d) 700
questions.trap_why: they multiply by 1.2, but real GDP removes inflation: 720 ÷ 120 × 100 = 600

questions.text: Calculate NNP at MP when NNP at FC is ₹15,000 crore, indirect taxes ₹450 crore, direct taxes ₹175 crore and subsidies ₹250 crore. (a) ₹15,025 crore (b) ₹15,200 crore (c) ₹15,275 crore (d) ₹15,525 crore
questions.trap_why: direct taxes play no part in moving from factor cost to market price: 15,000 + 450 − 250 = 15,200

questions.text: Hours of labour 1, 2, 3 give total product 20, 50, 90 (marginal product of the 3rd hour is 40). What is the average product for the third hour of labour? (a) 25 (b) 30 (c) 35 (d) 40
questions.trap_why: 40 is the marginal product of the 3rd hour; average product is total ÷ hours = 90 ÷ 3 = 30
